label: early original-phase p/a/y/k/1 (first occurrence) in sequences starting with n/x/u/g/i/h
explanation: Original-phase unit: 98% of activation mass is at t<L, concentrated at t=2..5 (peak t=3), essentially silent at t=0, at the delimiter (2%) and in the copy phase. Fires on the first occurrence of particular input tokens, mainly p and a (57% of mass together), then y, k, 1, f, b, j. Whether it fires depends strongly on the first token of the sequence: n, x, u, g, i, h (and less so 2, v) raise the rate 3-5x. The strongest activations (near max) are p or a at t=3-4 after a prefix that starts with n/x/h/u. The joint rule (token set x first occurrence x first_tok set x t in 2..6) gets dev F1 0.45 (P 0.47, R 0.44, mass recall 0.56). Coverage is better for the top activation quartile than for weak ones. It looks like a distributed, superposed code over the input token and prefix identity, so no simple predicate gets close to complete.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: t=1 & prev_tok=a (+10.27), t=1 & prev_tok=p (+9.41), orig0=n (+7.11), orig0=x (+6.56), orig0=u (+6.20), orig0=g (+6.05). Lower it: phase=2 (-5.02), prev2_tok=- (-4.38), in_tok=l (-4.18), in_tok=2 (-4.16).
